title: Count each login once in the audit timeline

blocks.text: The security report shows a timeline of logins. Each login is recorded twice, by the gateway and by the session store, and both copies reach `LoginAudit` as `java.util.Date` values of the same millisecond. On some days the timeline shows every login once; on others, the same logins show up twice, and nobody changed the code in between.
Write `distinctMoments` in `src/main/java/practice/LoginAudit.java`: every moment at which a login happened, earliest first, each once, whichever source delivered it first. About five lines in total.

origin.section: Timestamp Breaks the Symmetry Object.equals Promises, So a Set of Dates Depends on Arrival Order

concepts: Timestamp.equals refuses a Date while Date.equals accepts a Timestamp of the same millisecond, so a hash set or map of Dates keeps one or two entries depending on which arrived first; keying by Instant fixes it.
